intended_object: The standard weight-basis vector v_i of the (n+1)-dimensional irreducible sl₂-module V(n) = K^{n+1}, with the usual convention v_i = 0 for i > n. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The module `Sl2Std K n` is `Fin (n + 1) → K`, and `basis K n` is `Pi.basisFun`, the coordinate basis. `basisVector K n i` returns the i-th coordinate vector when i ≤ n and 0 otherwise, which is what the docstring describes. The lemma `basisVector_apply` confirms its j-th coordinate is 1 if j = i and 0 otherwise. Setting v_i = 0 outside the weight string is the standard convention in sl₂ representation theory (for example, Humphreys sets v_{-1} = 0 and v_{n+1} = 0), and it makes the action formulas hold uniformly. The definition only needs a commutative ring K, which is the natural generality for this module. It is a particular vector of a particular module, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib does not define this ℕ-indexed, zero-extended family on its own; the nearest construction is `Pi.single i 1` / `Pi.basisFun`, which this definition wraps.
